Telehealth expansion is exactly the kind of innovation that crushes bureaucratic bloat while serving Americans who need it most. Rural communities shouldn’t have to fund D.C.’s endless healthcare red tape just to see a doctor. 

But let’s be clear—real progress means cutting the waste fueling hospital monopolies and Big Pharma price gouging. Every dollar saved by streamlining care via telehealth should go back to taxpayers, not get funneled into another D.C. slush fund. 

The last admin talked about “access” while letting 340B programs get exploited by corporate hospitals. This legislation must ensure savings actually reach patients, not administrators.

Medical bureaucracy is the enemy of life-saving innovation. The Honor Our Living Donors Act (S.957) cuts through the red tape by banning insurers from jacking up premiums on selfless donors—finally aligning policy with common sense. Taxpayers win too: every transplant saves Medicare $150k/year versus dialysis.

But let’s not stop there—HHS wasted $367M on the Acacia Center contract alone before cancellation. Imagine redirecting that bloat to scale donor protections nationally.

The system works when government gets out of the way.
